subject: Guarantee: we won't learn from your content — archive lifecycle Q&A
messages:
From: Ellie Chen <ellie.chen@payco.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@payco.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Quick confirmation: do you train on customer content? + archive questions

Hi Marissa,

We are finalizing language for PayCo's procurement review and need explicit, plain-language confirmation on two items before legal signs off:

1) Do you ever use customer-provided content (API requests, uploaded files, transcripts) to train or improve Redwood models (either internal research models or production models)?
2) How are archived artifacts handled — snapshots, backups, and long-term cold storage? Are there any exceptions where archived data might be used for modeling or research?

We need definitive contract wording we can include (preferably one short paragraph) plus any notes on retention windows, tombstone/delete timelines, and whether you can provide a deletion certificate.

Thanks — appreciate a concise answer so I can move this to our procurement team.

— Ellie
Ellie Chen
Head of Platform Security, PayCo
ellie.chen@payco.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: do you train on customer content? + archive questions

Hi Ellie — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: by default, Redwood does NOT use customer content to train or improve our models. We can also provide contract language and deletion evidence on request.

High-level bullets (summary):
- Modeling: Customer content is not incorporated into Redwood model training unless the customer explicitly opts in to a modeling program (we never train on customer data by default).
- Telemetry & Debugging: Short-lived telemetry (metrics, sampling of error traces) is kept for service health and debugging; retention defaults are short (see below).
- Snapshots/backups: We create engineering snapshots for debugging and disaster recovery; those are governed by a separate retention/tombstone process and are not used for model training.
- Deletion flow: We support account-level deletion requests. Deletion triggers tombstoning and a background purge; we can provide a certificate of deletion once purge completes.

I've attached our latest data use policy for wording you can drop into contracts. Looping Mina for the detailed security/compliance language and Ben for commercial/contract implications.

Attachments: redwood-data-use-policy-v3.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: do you train on customer content? + archive questions

Hi Ellie — adding the detail your procurement and security teams usually ask for. Quoted below is the plain contract paragraph we recommend; beneath that are the operational specifics.

Recommended contract language (single paragraph):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content to train, improve, or derive models, machine learning systems, or generative model weights without the Customer's prior written consent. Customer Content will be accessed only as necessary to provide the Services and in accordance with the applicable Data Retention and Deletion policies set forth in this Agreement."

Operational details:
- Scope: "Customer Content" = all text, files, prompts, attachments, and transcripts submitted by the customer under the account. Internal telemetry (e.g., anonymized request latency metrics) is excluded from this definition when used solely for service reliability.
- Opt-in training: Any program that uses customer data for modeling requires an explicit opt-in workflow, documented consent, and a separate data handling agreement (we maintain an auditable consent log).
- Short-term traces: Error traces and request metadata used for debugging are retained by default for 30 days and are not material for model training (access controls restrict engineering access; audit logs record access).
- Snapshots & backups: Engineering snapshots taken for debugging may be retained for up to 90 days. Cold backups (disaster recovery) may be kept longer (up to 12 months) but are encrypted and stored in immutable backup storage with strict access controls; these backups are also excluded from any training pipelines.
- Deletion/tombstone: Upon a deletion request we tombstone the primary records immediately; tombstoned data is purged from live stores within 30 days and from backups/snapshots according to the retention matrix (we perform a best-effort purge of deletable data from backups during the next scheduled retention cycle). We provide a deletion certificate on completion of the purge.
- Forensic/evidence: We can provide audit logs (who accessed what and when) and deletion certificates. For enterprise customers we offer an extended evidence package (signed attestation + S3 object list + purge log) as part of the enterprise onboarding.
- Controls: KMS for tenant keys, HSM optional, SOC 2 Type II, regular third-party audits.

Exceptions & caveats:
- Legal holds: Data subject to lawful preservation requests (e.g., subpoenas) will be retained as required and excluded from deletion until release — we log and notify customers as per policy.
- Debug-only snapshots: In rare debugging incidents we may create short-lived copies; these are flagged as "debug" and subject to accelerated deletion (<=90 days).

Attachments: snapshot-retention-matrix.xlsx (gives the exact TTLs by artifact type)

If you'd like, we can produce a one-paragraph SLA-friendly redline for your contract team and a short vendor-security FAQ tailored for PayCo.

Best,

Thanks all — short commercial notes to close this out for procurement:

- We can accept Mina's recommended contract paragraph verbatim.
- For standard enterprise terms we include the non-training guarantee at no extra charge; for customers requesting guaranteed accelerated purge from backups or a signed deletion attestation within a compressed timeline we offer a small one-time professional-services fee (we've priced that in the past at $5k–$15k depending on scope).
- If PayCo wants an absolute contractual representation covering backups and cold archives (not just a policy statement), we can add the specific retention windows and the deletion certificate SLA into Schedule A of the Master Services Agreement.

Next steps: Marissa — I recommend we: (1) send Ellie a redline (one-paragraph) and the snapshot-retention-matrix, (2) offer PayCo the optional evidence package description and cost, and (3) propose contract language for legal.
